Instructions for setting up pre-commit hooks and testing CDK additions in a development environment.

# Purpose
This documentation provides instructions for setting up and using development tools and infrastructure testing within a monorepo for a software project. It details the use of `pre-commit` and `Ruff` to enforce code quality and consistency by automatically running linters and formatters on code changes. Users are guided through installing `pre-commit` hooks, which are configured in the `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file, to ensure these checks occur with each commit. Additionally, the document explains the use of a `test-in-dev` CDK stack for testing infrastructure changes in a development environment. This stack allows developers to manually test infrastructure additions without automated deployment, with instructions on how to deploy changes using the `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT` variable. The document also includes guidance on using AWS constructs and stacks to model and deploy application components, emphasizing the separation of logical units into constructs for better reuse and deployment flexibility.
# Content Summary
The document provides instructions for setting up and maintaining code quality in a Driver AI monorepo using pre-commit hooks and Ruff for linting and formatting. Developers are instructed to install pre-commit globally using Python or Homebrew, and then install the pre-commit hooks defined in the `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file by navigating to the root of the monorepo and executing `pre-commit install`. These hooks automatically run Ruff and other linters during commits to ensure code quality and consistency. Developers can also manually run pre-commit hooks on all files using `pre-commit run --all-files`.

Additionally, the document describes a process for testing infrastructure changes using a `test-in-dev` CDK stack. This stack allows developers to test additions to the infrastructure manually, as the current setup does not support fully automated environment creation. Developers can modify the `test_in_dev_stack.py` file and deploy changes using the command `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT=test-in-dev cdk deploy`. The mapping of the `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT` variable to different stacks is managed in the `./cdk_app.py` file, which can be customized for new test environments.

The document also includes guidance from AWS on using constructs and stacks. Constructs should represent logical units of an application, while stacks should describe how these constructs are composed and connected for deployment. This approach enhances the reuse potential of infrastructure and provides flexibility in deployment scenarios.
